database_summary: Airline operations dataset containing reference data for aircrafts and airports, transactional/event tables for bookings, tickets, ticket_flights and boarding_passes, flight schedule and status in flights, and seat configurations. Mix of descriptive reference/dimension tables (aircrafts_data, airports_data, seats), event/transactional grains (bookings, tickets, ticket_flights, boarding_passes), and scheduled/current-state records (flights). Useful for queries about bookings, ticketing, passenger-seat assignments, flight schedules and status, and aircraft/airport lookups.

accepted.name: flights_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  status,
  aircraft_code,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival
FROM flights
accepted.description: Normalized projection of flights with deterministic columns and nullable-safe aliases. Use this as the canonical flights relation for joins and downstream analytics (scheduling, punctuality, joins to ticket segments). | Use for: flight on-time/delay analysis; join tickets/ticket_flights to flights; flight schedule listings and filtering by airport or status

accepted.name: flights_delay_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  aircraft_code,
  scheduled_departure,
  actual_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  actual_arrival,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_departure IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_departure IS NOT NULL
    THEN CAST((julianday(actual_departure) - julianday(scheduled_departure)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS departure_delay_minutes,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_arrival IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_arrival IS NOT NULL
    THEN CAST((julianday(actual_arrival) - julianday(scheduled_arrival)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arrival_delay_minutes
FROM flights
accepted.description: Per-flight derived delay measures: departure_delay_minutes and arrival_delay_minutes computed when actual timestamps are present. Useful to summarize punctuality or compute aggregates by aircraft, route, or date. | Use for: compute average delay by route/aircraft/day; identify delayed flights; percent on-time vs delayed

accepted.name: ticket_segments_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tf.ticket_no,
  tf.flight_id,
  tf.fare_conditions,
  tf.amount,
  t.book_ref,
  t.passenger_id,
  b.book_date,
  b.total_amount
FROM ticket_flights tf
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON tf.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
LEFT JOIN bookings b ON t.book_ref = b.book_ref
accepted.description: Denormalized one-row-per ticket segment combining ticket_flights with ticket and booking metadata. Preserves ticket and booking keys for downstream aggregation by passenger or booking. | Use for: revenue per ticket segment; passenger-level spending and segments; join segments to flights/schedules

accepted.name: boarding_with_seat_and_ticket
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  bp.ticket_no,
  bp.flight_id,
  bp.boarding_no,
  bp.seat_no,
  t.passenger_id,
  t.book_ref,
  s.aircraft_code AS seats_aircraft_code,
  s.seat_no AS seats_seat_no,
  s.fare_conditions AS seats_fare_conditions
FROM boarding_passes bp
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON bp.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
LEFT JOIN seats s ON s.aircraft_code = (
    SELECT aircraft_code FROM flights f WHERE f.flight_id = bp.flight_id
  ) AND s.seat_no = bp.seat_no
accepted.description: One row per boarding_pass enriched with ticket passenger and seat configuration (when available). Helpful to reconcile assigned seat_no with aircraft seat map and fare class. | Use for: seat assignment consistency checks; boarding lists and passenger-seat lookups; analyse fare class distribution by actual assigned seats

accepted.name: aircrafts_reference
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  aircraft_code,
  model,
  range
FROM aircrafts_data
accepted.description: Pass-through of aircrafts_data providing aircraft_code and model and range. Keep model as-is (jsonb) so callers decide localization. Use for joins and aircraft-level summaries. | Use for: lookup aircraft model or range; join aircraft attributes to flights for capacity/range analysis

accepted.name: airports_reference
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  airport_code,
  airport_name,
  city,
  coordinates,
  timezone
FROM airports_data
accepted.description: Pass-through of airports_data exposing airport_code and localized blobs. Consumers should extract language from airport_name and city jsonb. Useful for joins and geospatial lookups. | Use for: airport lookups by code; map flights by departure/arrival airport coordinates; filter flights by timezone or city

accepted.name: flight_rank_by_time
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  departure_airport,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY departure_airport ORDER BY scheduled_departure) AS departure_rank
FROM flights
accepted.description: Ranks flights per departure_airport by scheduled_departure time. Exposes departure_rank so callers can filter for earliest or latest N flights per airport without hardcoding a limit. | Use for: top-N earliest flights per airport; sampling flights around schedule boundaries

accepted.name: bookings_revenue_by_date
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(book_date) AS book_date,
  COUNT(*) AS bookings_count,
  SUM(total_amount) AS bookings_total_amount
FROM bookings
GROUP BY DATE(book_date)
accepted.description: Daily aggregates of booking revenue and counts by book_date (date-truncated). Useful for trends, time-series, and rolling analyses. Does not assume timezone conversion; keeps book_date as source provides. | Use for: daily revenue/time trends; compare booking volume vs revenue

accepted.name: passenger_segment_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.passenger_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tf.flight_id) AS segments_count,
  SUM(tf.amount) AS segments_total_amount
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN ticket_flights tf ON t.ticket_no = tf.ticket_no
GROUP BY t.passenger_id
accepted.description: Counts and total amount per passenger (passenger_id) across their ticket segments. Useful to rank passengers by spend or segments and to detect high-value customers. | Use for: identify top passengers by spend or segments; customer lifetime/usage summaries
